articles.title: AI Chargeback Disputes: How Small Ecommerce Stores Automate Evidence and Win
articles.excerpt: In March 2025 I watched a client lose $1,180 to a single Visa dispute she never fought. Not because the customer was right. Because she never opened the dispute portal at all. The notification sat in…
articles.body: In March 2025 I watched a client lose $1,180 to a single Visa dispute she never fought. Not because the customer was right. Because she never opened the dispute portal at all. The notification sat in her payment processor inbox for 12 days, the deadline passed, and the money was gone. That one lazy moment convinced her to spend a weekend automating the whole thing. Nine months later her store's chargeback win rate sits at 71% against an industry benchmark of roughly 44% for merchants who fight their disputes at all, per Chargebacks911's dispute data . The real baseline is worse: most small merchants never respond, and a non-response is an automatic loss. What AI Actually Changes About Chargeback Disputes Chargeback response work is paperwork with a clock attached.
articles.author: Veduis

articles.title: AWS Trust in Depth: Five Layers for Agent Autonomy Without Losing Control
articles.excerpt: Enterprise leaders want AI agents to do more work. They also don't trust them to act correctly every time. This tension blocks production deployment. AWS's Trust in Depth framework addresses it with f…
articles.body: Enterprise leaders want AI agents to do more work. They also don't trust them to act correctly every time. This tension blocks production deployment. AWS's Trust in Depth framework addresses it with five layers: scope, know, bound, observe, and prove. Each layer targets a specific failure mode. Together they let agents act autonomously when actions can be verified and reserve human judgment for decisions that need it. The Five Layers Scope constrains what resources and APIs an agent can access before it starts reasoning. This is pre-execution access control. You define allowed tools, data sources, and external services at orchestration time. If the agent tries to call an out-of-scope API, the request fails before the LLM even sees the response.

articles.title: Solid Queue 1.6.0 Fiber Workers: How Rails Turned Concurrency Primitives into Agent Job Orchestration
articles.excerpt: Solid Queue 1.6.0 ships with fiber-based workers, replacing the traditional thread-per-job model with cooperative multitasking. This is not a cosmetic change. Fibers let you run hundreds of concurrent…
articles.body: Solid Queue 1.6.0 ships with fiber-based workers, replacing the traditional thread-per-job model with cooperative multitasking. This is not a cosmetic change. Fibers let you run hundreds of concurrent jobs in a single OS thread, cutting memory overhead and context-switching costs. For agent workflows that spawn many lightweight tasks (API calls, LLM token streaming, webhook dispatches), this changes the economics of job orchestration. Rails already had Active Job and Solid Queue for database-backed job queues. The new fiber mode integrates the Async gem, which provides non-blocking I/O primitives. Instead of blocking a thread while waiting for HTTP responses or database queries, a fiber yields control back to the scheduler.

articles.title: Returning samples from a Mars moon: Inside the science of Japan's bold MMX mission
articles.excerpt: Japan's mission to Mars' moons could answer a decades old question dividing the origins of Phobos and Deimos between two conflicting theories, and make history as the first spacecraft to return to Ear…
articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. MMX is scheduled to launch on an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center on Monday (Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan, Oct.

articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
